newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to develop hydroelectric plants - minister.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to develop hydroelectric plants - minister.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim energy minister said on Wednesday priority would be given to developing hydroelectric power stations as part of efforts to lessen dependence on nuclear power production.
Georgi Stoilov said the hydroelectric power could compete with the production of the country's Kozloduy nuclear power plant, which usually meets 40 percent of the country's power needs.
"Despite the great improvements which have been made on the Kozloduy (oldest) reactors...the danger is greater than the socially accepted risk," Stoilov told a ministry meeting.

Bulgaria, which relies on antiquated thermal power plants for half of its energy, suffers from a lack of water and continuing drought has lead to severe rationing in 1994 in many parts of the country, including the capital Sofia.

The European Commission appealed to the Bulgarian government last December to continue improving the safety of four of its Soviet-made reactors while it seeks alternative resources before closing these reactors.
Stoilov said priority would also be given to energy efficiency.
